title: Supplemental Balance Allowances by Stage (Placed Consumer Accounts)
content:
Client Services schedule for **Placed Consumer Accounts**: the room each placement stage gives a client to add a supplemental balance, meaning an increase in the same debt, to an account already placed.

| Stage | Supplemental window (calendar days after the placement date) | Most supplemental additions on one account | Cap on cumulative additions (percent of the placed balance) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Early-Out Placement | 90 | 4 | 50% |
| Primary Placement | 60 | 2 | 25% |
| Secondary Placement | 30 | 1 | 10% |
| Tertiary Placement | 30 | 1 | 10% |
| Warehouse Placement | 0 (none accepted) | 0 | 0% |
| Legal Review Placement | 0 (none accepted) | 0 | 0% |

## Column definitions

- **Supplemental window**: the calendar days after the placement date during which a client may add a supplemental balance. A window of 0 means the stage accepts no supplemental balance.
- **Most supplemental additions**: the largest number of supplemental additions one account may carry.
- **Cap on cumulative additions**: the largest total of all supplemental additions on the account, stated as a percentage of the placed balance.

## Hypothetical figures worked from the table

*The placed balances below are invented for illustration.*

| Stage | Hypothetical placed balance | Cumulative cap in dollars |
|---|---|---|
| Early-Out Placement | $800.00 | 50% of $800.00, that is $400.00 |
| Primary Placement | $1200.00 | 25% of $1200.00, that is $300.00 |
| Secondary Placement | $900.00 | 10% of $900.00, that is $90.00 |

Warehouse Placement and Legal Review Placement carry zero in all three columns, so no supplemental balance is ever added at those stages.
